operation.new:
Reading the :attr:`port` attribute will raise a :exc:`ValueError` if
   an invalid port is specified in the URL.  See section
   :ref:`urlparse-result-object` for more information on the result object.
   Unlike other attributes, :attr:`port` is not validated when the result
   object is constructed by :func:`urlparse` or :func:`urlsplit`; the
   exception is raised only when the :attr:`port` attribute is first
   accessed.  A port is valid if it is an integer in the range 0 through
   65535 (inclusive).  Any other value in the port position of the
   *netloc* raises a :exc:`ValueError` when :attr:`port` is accessed.

   .. doctest::

      >>> from urllib.parse import urlparse
      >>> # Valid boundary ports are accepted
      >>> urlparse("http://example.com:0/").port
      0
      >>> urlparse("http://example.com:65535/").port
      65535
      >>> # Out-of-range port: construction succeeds, but .port raises
      >>> u = urlparse("http://example.com:65536/")
      >>> u.netloc
      'example.com:65536'
      >>> u.port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
      ValueError: Port out of range 0-65535
      >>> # Non-integer port: same lazy validation
      >>> urlparse("http://example.com:abc/").port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
      ValueError: Port could not be cast to integer value as 'abc'
